title: Senescent fibroblasts secrete an inflammatory program enriched for IL-6 and IL-8
abstract: We profiled the secretome of replicatively senescent human fibroblasts and observed marked upregulation of pro-inflammatory factors, most prominently IL-6 and IL-8. This senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) was sustained over weeks in culture. The findings indicate that senescent cells are not metabolically silent but actively shape their local environment through cytokine secretion.

title: p16INK4a accumulation tracks chronological age across human tissues
abstract: Expression of the cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor p16INK4a increased with donor age in multiple tissue types. p16INK4a is widely used as a marker of cellular senescence, and its accumulation is consistent with a rising senescent-cell burden in aged tissue. We discuss the limits of any single marker for identifying senescence in vivo.

title: Clearance of p16-positive senescent cells delays age-related tissue dysfunction in mice
abstract: Using a genetic system to eliminate p16INK4a-expressing cells, we found that clearing senescent cells delayed the onset of several age-related phenotypes in mice. Removal reduced local inflammation and improved tissue function. These results support the hypothesis that senescent cells contribute causally to aspects of aging, though translation to humans remains untested.

title: Rapamycin-mediated mTOR inhibition extends lifespan in a mouse cohort
abstract: Chronic administration of rapamycin, an inhibitor of mTOR, was associated with increased median lifespan in treated mice relative to controls. mTOR is a central nutrient-sensing kinase and a negative regulator of autophagy. The lifespan effect was accompanied by changes in markers of autophagy, suggesting a possible mechanistic link that the study did not establish causally.

title: Declining autophagic flux with age and partial restoration of healthspan markers
abstract: Autophagic flux declined with age in the tissues we examined. Genetic restoration of autophagy improved several healthspan-associated markers without extending maximum lifespan. We interpret autophagy as one contributor among many to age-related decline, and caution against treating any single pathway as sufficient.

title: ATG7-dependent autophagy promotes establishment of the senescence secretory phenotype
abstract: We report that autophagy is required for full induction of the SASP during oncogene-induced senescence. Knockdown of ATG7 blunted secretion of IL-6 and slowed onset of senescence markers. In this model autophagy promotes, rather than restrains, the senescent program. We note the result appears to conflict with reports in other cell systems.

title: Loss of LC3B-mediated autophagy accelerates senescence and amplifies the SASP
abstract: In primary human fibroblasts, impairing autophagy by depleting LC3B or ATG7 accelerated the onset of senescence and increased IL-6 secretion. Here autophagy restrains senescence, in apparent tension with reports that autophagy is required to establish the SASP. We suggest the direction of the effect is context dependent and not yet resolved.

title: A senolytic combination reduces senescent-cell burden and circulating IL-6
abstract: Treatment with a senolytic combination reduced markers of senescent-cell burden and lowered circulating IL-6 in an aged mouse model. Effects on physical function were modest. We frame senolytics as a promising but unproven strategy and emphasize that no clinical efficacy claim is supported by these preclinical data.

title: The p53-p21 axis enforces DNA-damage-induced senescence
abstract: Persistent DNA damage signaling activated p53 and its transcriptional target p21, driving a stable cell-cycle arrest characteristic of senescence. Loss of p21 attenuated arrest. The work places the p53-p21 axis upstream of senescence induction in this stress model, complementing the p16INK4a pathway.

title: SIRT1 decline in senescent cells and attenuation of inflammatory secretion upon its activation
abstract: SIRT1 protein levels decreased in senescent fibroblasts. Pharmacological activation of SIRT1 reduced secretion of IL-6 without reversing the cell-cycle arrest. The data position SIRT1 as a modulator of the inflammatory SASP rather than of senescence growth arrest itself.

title: FOXO3 longevity-associated variants and cellular stress resistance
abstract: Carriers of FOXO3 longevity-associated variants showed greater resistance to oxidative stress in derived cell lines. FOXO3 is a forkhead transcription factor repeatedly linked to human longevity in population studies. We report an association, not a mechanism, and note that genotype effects were small.

title: Loss of nuclear Lamin B1 as a candidate biomarker of cellular senescence
abstract: Senescent cells showed reduced nuclear Lamin B1 (LMNB1) across induction methods. Lamin B1 loss complemented p16INK4a and SA-beta-galactosidase as a marker, though specificity was imperfect. We recommend combining markers rather than relying on any one to call senescence.

title: SASP-derived IL-6 drives paracrine senescence and chronic low-grade inflammation
abstract: Conditioned medium from senescent cells induced senescence markers in neighboring cells, an effect partly attributable to IL-6. We connect the SASP to chronic low-grade inflammation, often termed inflammaging, observed in aged tissue. The paracrine effect was incomplete and dose dependent.

title: Caloric restriction activates autophagy via mTOR inhibition and improves metabolic markers
abstract: Caloric restriction lowered mTOR signaling and increased autophagic flux, accompanied by improved metabolic markers in treated animals. The intervention did not measurably alter senescent-cell markers in the same tissues. We treat the autophagy and senescence pathways as distinct axes that may intersect but were not jointly resolved here.

title: Senescent-cell accumulation is associated with multiple age-related conditions: an observational survey
abstract: Across the datasets we surveyed, markers of senescent-cell accumulation co-occurred with several age-related conditions. These are observational associations and do not establish causation. We highlight the absence of standardized senescence definitions as a barrier to comparison across studies.

title: Single-cell profiling reveals heterogeneity of senescent-cell states
abstract: Single-cell transcriptomics of induced senescent populations revealed substantial heterogeneity, including variable expression of p16INK4a and SASP genes such as IL-6. The results argue against a single canonical senescent state and complicate marker-based identification. We provide the analysis as a methodological resource.

title: Partial reprogramming reduces senescence markers in cultured cells: a hypothesis-generating study
abstract: Transient expression of reprogramming factors reduced p16INK4a and restored some youthful expression patterns in cultured cells, without full dedifferentiation. We present this as hypothesis-generating; effects on tissue function in vivo were not tested and safety is unaddressed. No therapeutic claim is intended.

title: Senolytic interventions and inflammatory markers: a meta-analysis with mixed results
abstract: Pooling preclinical and early-stage studies, the effect of senolytic interventions on circulating IL-6 and related inflammatory markers was heterogeneous, with several studies showing no significant change. Effect sizes were imprecise and study quality varied. We conclude the evidence is currently inconclusive and discourage overinterpretation.
